newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas extends gains with heat, stock refills.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas extends gains with heat, stock refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to strengthen Tuesday as lingering heat on the Gulf Coast and storage demand kept buyers clutched onto the market, industry sources said.
In south Texas, prices gained another nine cents to the high-$2.50s as temperature highs climbed into the mid-to-high 90s F.
At the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices at Henry Hub rose an average of five cents to the low-$2.60s.
Triggering some additional buying, one Texas trader said, were balancing needs on the Gulf pipes following a light volume bidweek.
Strong buying interest in the Gulf also filtered into the west Texas market, where Permian prices jumped another four cents to the high-$2.40s. San Juan prices were quoted at $2.37-2.42.
At the southern California border, prices rose a similar amount to the mid-$2.50s.
In the Midwest, where most temperatures are hovering below normal, prices edged up two cents to $2.45-2.47. Chicago city-gate was also higher at $2.63-2.68.
In the East, prices at New York city gate were quoted at $2.78-2.81, up two to four cents from Monday.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report ranged from 60 to 90 bcf, versus a 93 bcf build a year ago.
